src:bnl-about-history-page.excerpt: Brookhaven National Laboratory was established in 1947 on the eastern end of Long Island at the former site of the U.S. Army's Camp Upton.
src:bnl-about-history-page.title: BNL | Our History

src:bnl-about-page.excerpt: Brookhaven Science Associates, a partnership between Stony Brook University and Battelle, and six core universities: Columbia, Cornell, Harvard, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Princeton, and Yale, manages and operates the laboratory for the DOE's Office of Science.
src:bnl-about-page.title: BNL | About Brookhaven National Laboratory

src:bnl-newsroom-eic-transformation-2026.excerpt: Work begins today at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Brookhaven National Laboratory to remove components from the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) ... the first step in transforming the renowned collider into ... the world's only fully polarized Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). One of RHIC's ion storage rings, the pre-accelerator chain, and a large detector hall will be reused for the new facility.
src:bnl-newsroom-eic-transformation-2026.title: Transformation of RHIC to EIC Begins

src:bnl-newsroom-full-energy-2001.excerpt: The new collisions, at 100 GeV per nucleon, will deposit more energy into the collisions, raising the temperature higher.
src:bnl-newsroom-full-energy-2001.title: RHIC Resumes Operation With First Full-Energy Collisions

src:bnl-newsroom-run22-2021.excerpt: This year's run will take place at the highest collision energy: 500 billion electron volts (GeV) per colliding proton pair.
src:bnl-newsroom-run22-2021.title: Start-up of 22nd Run at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC)

src:bnl-newsroom-run23-2023.excerpt: 200 billion electron volts, or GeV, per colliding pair of nuclei ... the last 200 GeV gold-gold run at RHIC was in 2016.
src:bnl-newsroom-run23-2023.title: RHIC Gets Ready to Smash Gold Ions for Run 23

src:bnl-rhic-ags-page.excerpt: The AGS receives protons and other ions from the AGS Booster and delivers them to the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider after acceleration. It can accelerate 70 trillion protons with every pulse, and heavy ions such as gold and iron.
src:bnl-rhic-ags-page.title: BNL | RHIC | Alternating Gradient Synchrotron

src:bnl-rhic-booster-page.excerpt: Construction of the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (AGS) Booster was begun in 1986 and completed in 1991.
src:bnl-rhic-booster-page.title: Booster Synchrotron (RHIC accelerator complex)

src:bnl-rhic-complex-page.excerpt: RHIC's 2.4-mile ring had six intersection points where its two rings of accelerating magnets crossed, allowing the particle beams to collide. Detectors were originally located at four of these 'interaction regions,' and later, at only two.
src:bnl-rhic-complex-page.title: BNL | RHIC | The Collider Complex

src:bnl-rhic-linac-page.excerpt: The Linac is capable of producing a negatively charged hydrogen beam of up to 200 million electron-volts (MeV) energy and 135 microampere average current.
src:bnl-rhic-linac-page.title: 200 MeV Linear Accelerator (RHIC accelerator complex)

src:bnl-rhic-page.excerpt: The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC), operational from 2000-2026 ... RHIC was the first machine in the world capable of colliding ions as heavy as gold ... RHIC collided beams of polarized protons to investigate the 'missing' spin of the proton.
src:bnl-rhic-page.title: BNL | Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC)

C 50, 043001 (2026) (INSPIRE literature id 3084402, DOI 10.1088/1674-1137/ae3dc1); full text confirms the as-built PMT counts (17596 20-inch PMTs: 4939 dynode-PMTs + 12657 MCP-PMTs; 25587 3-inch PMTs), the detailed construction timeline (civil construction of the underground lab started January 2015; SS support structure installation started 19 December 2021; PMT/electronics installation 23 October 2022 to 17 December 2024; water filling 18 December 2024 to 2 February 2025; LS exchange 8 February 2025 to 22 August 2025; physics data taking started 26 August 2025), and an overburden of 1800 m.w.e.

src:reactor-solar-verify-reno-final-2024.excerpt: RENO's final/complete-dataset oscillation measurement. Abstract states: 'The experiment has measured the amplitude and frequency of reactor anti-electron-neutrinos oscillations at the Hanbit nuclear power plant, Younggwang, Korea, since August 2011. As of March 2023, the data acquisition was completed after a total of 3800 live days of detector operation.' Confirms RENO's data-taking start (August 2011, matching the 2012 discovery paper) and its end (March 2023).
src:reactor-solar-verify-reno-final-2024.title: Measurement of reactor antineutrino oscillation amplitude and frequency using 3800 days of complete data sample of the RENO experiment
